classification.basis: Complete transection of a main duct (operative history C16; corroborated by ERCP cut-off and MRCP) places the injury in Strasberg type E. The MRCP stump measurement is 25 mm below an intact confluence; C14 Table 2: stump > 2 cm from the confluence = Bismuth I = Strasberg E1. Every other rule is excluded by a named absent finding (no minor-duct leak, no aberrant-duct occlusion/transection/involvement, no lateral injury, confluence intact, stump >= 20 mm), each of which the checker re-evaluates from the findings.

adjudication.decided_by: Case-author adjudication against the cited classification and criteria (C14, C2), recorded here in full so any reviewer can re-derive it. The classification itself is not asserted here: it is computed by the strasberg_bismuth block from the staged findings and the stump measurement, and the checker recomputes it. This is not an external adjudication: the design/07 review gate (>= 2 named independent reviewers) is UNMET for this case, as the review block states.
adjudication.diagnosis_label: Major bile duct injury — complete transection of the common bile duct, Strasberg E1 / Bismuth I

evidence_chain.role: The index operation's Theatre debrief: CBD clipped t=1860 s, transected t=1920 s, Stewart-Way class III, recognised intraoperatively, drain-and-refer
Bilirubin 6.8 mg/dL — rises in complete occlusion
Dilated intrahepatic ducts above the injury
Complete transection at the clip level; stump 25 mm below an intact confluence

excluded.basis: Excluded by imaging and by the one quantified update: MRCP shows no stone in any duct (f.mrcp-no-stone; LR- 0.0794 from C15 carries the workbench posterior to 0.0195, below the 0.02 rule-out line at stage 4), and the ERCP that was ordered to treat the presumed stone found a clear distal duct with the obstruction at the surgical clips (f.ercp-cutoff-at-clips). The stone hypothesis was reasonable at stage 1; by stage 4 nothing is left for it to stand on.

Excluded mechanically and clinically: the classification block's type-A rule fails on its own inputs (f.minor-duct-leak is an explicitly absent finding; the main duct is transected, not in continuity), there is no collection on ultrasound or MRCP (f.us-no-collection, f.mrcp-no-collection), and the clinical picture is obstruction-dominant — C14 notes jaundice is absent or mild in pure leak cases because cholestasis does not occur, while this patient's bilirubin is 6.8 mg/dL and rising.

Not met on TG18 (C2), mechanically, at every stage: group B is satisfied (bilirubin 6.8 >= 2; enzymes > 1.5x ULN) and group C is satisfied (biliary dilatation), but group A is not — no fever, WBC 8.9 (<= 10.0), CRP 8 mg/L (< 10). Suspected requires A plus one of B or C. The adjudication records this precisely because it is the case's live risk: an obstructed, undrained system is where cholangitis develops, and C14's delayed-repair pathway (statement 7.4) arms exactly that watch — if fever or inflammatory markers declare, the pathway changes to drainage (PTBD for complete obstruction) and antibiotics.

Excluded on the pattern and the history: the panel is cholestatic-dominant (f.cholestatic-pattern, flagged as an interpretation), the ducts are dilated (an obstructive picture), the anatomy is demonstrated, and there is no new drug exposure (f.no-new-drug-exposure). No LR was consulted for any of this and none is pretended.

adjudication.note: The workbench's evidence-updated board agrees with the adjudication (the adjudicated diagnosis is top-ranked at every stage), but the adjudication rests on the classification block and the operative history, not on the board — the board is a teaching instrument (see the lr_combination_rule in cases/parameters.json).

available_tests.note: C14 statement 6.2's panel. Settles TG18 cholangitis group B (C2) and establishes the cholestatic pattern.

available_tests.name: Abdominal ultrasound
available_tests.note: C14: ultrasound detects ductal dilation and fluid collections; it is the collection-hunting first look (statement 6.3 pairs it with CT). Its duct-stone sensitivity is not quantified here — none was consulted.

available_tests.name: ERCP with cholangiography
available_tests.note: Invasive, with the complication profile C14 lists (including post-ERCP pancreatitis). In a complete transection it can only ever show the distal duct up to the cut-off: it cannot opacity the proximal tree and cannot treat the injury (C14). Ordered by the learner at stage 2 as therapy for a presumed stone — the order the debrief examines.

available_tests.name: MRCP
available_tests.note: The gold standard for complete morphological evaluation of the biliary tree (C14): shows anatomy proximal and distal to the injury, supplies the stump measurement the Strasberg–Bismuth classification runs on, and answers the stone question with C15's characteristics.

findings.text: OPERATIVE HISTORY (the loop evidence item — read from theatre/debriefs/trace-02-divide-before-cvs.debrief.json, not retyped from memory; the checker re-reads that file and matches every fact stated here). At the index operation the structure believed to be the cystic duct was clipped at t=1860 s; the Theatre's misidentification resolution records the clipped structure as the common bile duct (Stewart-Way class I mechanism). At t=1920 s it was divided: bile-duct-injury, resolved structure duct.common-bile, Stewart-Way class III — a complete transection of the common bile duct. The injury was recognised during the operation (t=2100 s), the hepatobiliary team was called (t=2160 s), the decision at dp4 was drain-refer (t=2220 s), a closed drain was placed to the gallbladder fossa (microstep m7.6, t=2280 s), and the attempt's management score was 5/5. The attempt verdict was FAIL (checklist 32/64, safety gate 0/4). File SHA-256 7bb98df467e1e35992464b5ef4548d7b51e13c83bf6d0dbe27556b5a3af301b6 (recorded in theatre_link; the checker recomputes it).

criteria_roles: TG18 cholangitis group B context (C2) — the sign itself; the group is settled by the bilirubin lab
findings.text: Jaundice: sclerae and skin icteric, deepening since postoperative day 2 (case data). Cholestatic jaundice is the hallmark of the obstruction scenario in C14's postoperative presentation review.
Mild itching since day 3 (case data). Pruritus is listed among the most common clinical signs of the cholestatic/obstructive picture in C14.
Dark urine (choluria) and pale stools (fecal acholia) since day 3 (case data) — with jaundice and pruritus, the cholestatic symptom set C14 names for biliary obstruction.

Mild right upper quadrant discomfort, improving day by day; no distension, no nausea or vomiting (case data). Abdominal pain is one of C14 statement 6.1's alarm symptoms mandating prompt investigation after cholecystectomy.
ABSENT finding, recorded explicitly for the criteria evaluations: temperature 36.9 C at assessment and afebrile throughout the postoperative course (case data). No fever and no rigors at any stage.

The closed drain placed to the gallbladder fossa at the index operation (trace-02, microstep m7.6) remains in situ and drains about 40 mL per 24 h of bile-stained fluid, the volume falling each day (case data). A low, falling output: this is the obstruction scenario's drain picture, not the profuse persistent bile leakage C14 describes for an uncontrolled free leak.

No new regular medications since surgery; the only drug exposure is perioperative cefazolin prophylaxis (case data). Recorded against the hepatocellular-injury hypothesis; unquantified and weak — the laboratory pattern (f.cholestatic-pattern) is the real discriminator.

criteria_roles: TG18 cholangitis group B item B1 (C2) — satisfied (>= 2 mg/dL)
findings.text: Total bilirubin 6.8 mg/dL — far above reference (0.1–1.2, C8) and above the TG18 cholangitis cholestasis threshold of 2 mg/dL (C2). In complete occlusion of the bile duct, bilirubin rises (C14).

criteria_roles: TG18 cholangitis group B item B2 (C2) — satisfied (> 1.5x ULN)
findings.text: Alkaline phosphatase 520 U/L — about 4.0x the upper limit of reference (129 U/L, C8). ALP and total bilirubin are the early cholestasis markers named in C14.

criteria_roles: TG18 cholangitis group B item B2 (C2) — satisfied (> 1.5x ULN)
findings.text: ALT 96 U/L (2.7x the upper limit of 36, C8) and AST 88 U/L (2.7x the upper limit of 33, C8) — both above the TG18 cholangitis B-2 line of 1.5x ULN (C2), and both far below the bilirubin/ALP elevation in fold terms.

findings.lr_note: Pattern interpretation is the case author's reading of the panel (bilirubin 6.8 mg/dL and ALP 4.0x ULN dominant; transaminases 2.7x ULN), recorded as an interpretation, not a measurement. No likelihood ratio is taken for it: none was consulted, so the board is not moved by it. It acts in the adjudication and in the hepatocellular hypothesis's discriminator list.
findings.text: Laboratory pattern (case-author interpretation, flagged in lr_note): cholestatic — the obstruction enzymes dominate (bilirubin and ALP), with moderate transaminases. C14's biochemistry review: in stenosis or complete occlusion, bilirubin increases while aminotransferases are not the leading abnormality.

criteria_roles: TG18 cholangitis group C (C2) — biliary dilatation, satisfied
findings.text: Ultrasound: intrahepatic bile ducts dilated (case imaging report). Detecting ductal dilation is ultrasound's named role in C14's postoperative imaging review.

Ultrasound: no subhepatic or intra-abdominal fluid collection — no biloma (case imaging report). Ultrasound and CT are the collection-hunting modalities in C14 statement 6.3; a collection, if present, would be the percutaneous-drainage target under statement 7.4.

findings.lr_note: Unquantified: no test characteristic for ultrasound detection of duct stones was consulted in-session, so no LR is taken. The finding is recorded as weak negative evidence only; the stone question is settled by MRCP (f.mrcp-no-stone, LR from C15).
findings.text: Ultrasound: the distal common bile duct is incompletely visualised (bowel gas); no stone is identified in the visualised duct (case imaging report).

ERCP cholangiogram: a normal-calibre distal common bile duct opacifies up to an abrupt cut-off at surgical clips in the mid duct; no contrast passes the clips and the proximal tree is not opacified; no stone in the distal duct, none extracted (case procedure report). C14 states ERCP's limits exactly here: ducts upstream of an obstructing lesion are not visualised, and endoscopic therapy cannot bridge a transection of the common bile duct.

criteria_roles: Strasberg–Bismuth classification inputs: main_duct_transection; stump measurement (see measurements)
findings.text: MRCP: complete transection of the common bile duct at the surgical clip level, with loss of duct continuity; the remaining common hepatic duct stump measures 25 mm below an intact hepatic duct confluence (see measurements); intrahepatic ducts dilated above the injury (case imaging report). MRCP is the gold standard for complete morphological evaluation of the biliary tree and for localisation and classification of the injury (C14, statement 6.3 and KQ6 review). A HIDA scan was considered and not ordered: C14 records hepatobiliary scintigraphy as more sensitive for leaks but with poor spatial resolution and a specific pitfall in large duct defects (non-excretion misread), and it could not supply the stump measurement the classification needs.

lr.note: C15 is a single-centre retrospective study (n=691), not a meta-analysis; the LR is used with that limitation stated. Applied once, at stage 4.

findings.text: MRCP: no stone in any bile duct — no choledocholithiasis (case imaging report). This is the result C15's sensitivity/specificity describe, and its LR- is what carries the retained-stone hypothesis across the workbench rule-out line.

MRCP: the hepatic duct confluence is intact — the ceiling of the biliary confluence is preserved; right and left hepatic ducts communicate (case imaging report). In C14 Table 2's terms, the confluence ceiling is intact, not destroyed.

MRCP: no biloma and no intra-abdominal fluid collection (case imaging report) — corroborates f.us-no-collection. There is no collection for percutaneous drainage to target (C14 statement 7.4 applies drainage to collections 'whenever present').

ABSENT finding, recorded explicitly for the classification: MRCP shows no leak from the cystic duct stump and no leak from any minor duct in the liver bed (case imaging report). Strasberg type A is therefore excluded by the classification block, not by assertion.
ABSENT finding: no aberrant right sectoral duct is occluded (case imaging report). Strasberg type B excluded mechanically.
ABSENT finding: no aberrant right sectoral duct is transected or leaking (case imaging report). Strasberg type C excluded mechanically.

ABSENT finding: the main-duct injury is not a lateral (partial-circumference) defect; it is a complete transection (case imaging report; f.injury-main-duct-transection). Strasberg type D excluded mechanically.

ABSENT finding: no stricture or injury of an isolated right sectoral duct accompanies the main-duct injury (case imaging report). The Bismuth V / Strasberg E5 combination is therefore excluded mechanically.

ground_truth.diagnosis: Major bile duct injury — complete transection of the common bile duct at the index laparoscopic cholecystectomy (Theatre trace-02; Stewart-Way class III mechanism), classified Strasberg E1 / Bismuth I on this admission's MRCP, presenting as obstructive (cholestatic) jaundice on postoperative day 4
ground_truth.engine_state: No engine state is claimed. The physiology engine has no biliary perturbation (the missing biliary compartment recorded at Milestones 17, 18 and 20), so — unlike case 1 — this case declares no physiology_link at all rather than linking at a level that would be decorative. The gap is stated here, in the open.

hypotheses.defining_features: A major bile duct injury: complete loss of main-duct continuity with tissue loss — in C14's words, the pattern where 'the common bile duct is clipped and transected'. Strasberg type E, subdivided by the Bismuth level of the injury. This case's injury is not hypothetical: it is the Theatre trace-02 outcome, recognised at the index operation and referred (theatre_link, C16). What the workbench must still do is classify it (level) and exclude the rivals on this admission's evidence.

management.definitive_pathway: Roux-en-Y hepaticojejunostomy by the hepatobiliary team — the treatment of choice for major (Strasberg E) bile duct injury (C14 statement 4.2 and KQ3 review) — performed after a minimum of 3 weeks from the index operation, once the acute situation has resolved (C14 statement 7.4, the 72 h–3 week band this presentation falls in). ERCP has no definitive role: it cannot bridge a complete transection (C14), and its stage-3 performance in this case demonstrated exactly that limit. PTBD is held in reserve for the septic complete-obstruction scenario named in statement 7.4, which has not occurred.
management.disposition: The patient remains under the hepatobiliary team at the referral centre — the referral C14 statement 7.3 requires was already effected at the index operation (trace-02, dp4 drain-refer). No collection exists, so there is nothing for percutaneous drainage to target today; no infection is present, so no antibiotics are started (C14 KQ5: in biliary obstruction without bile leak or signs of sepsis, antibiotic therapy may not be required). The in-situ drain is monitored. Cholangitis surveillance is explicit: fever, rigors, or rising inflammatory markers move her onto the infected-obstruction pathway (drainage — PTBD is C14's named route for complete CBD obstruction — plus antibiotics).

measurements.name: Common hepatic duct stump below the confluence
measurements.note: MRCP measurement (case imaging report): distance from the hepatic duct confluence to the transection/clip level = the length of the remaining common hepatic duct stump. The Strasberg–Bismuth level thresholds are stated in centimetres in C14 Table 2 (stump > 2 cm = Bismuth I / Strasberg E1; stump < 2 cm = II / E2); the classification block compares this measurement against 20 mm and 1 mm. A case datum measured on the case's authored imaging, like every other case datum — the classification arithmetic on it is what the checker recomputes.

history: Four days ago she underwent the laparoscopic cholecystectomy that case.ruq-pain.001 handed to the Theatre (procedure proc.chole.lap). The operation as played in Theatre trace-02 is this case's operative history: the common bile duct was clipped at t=1860 s and transected at t=1920 s (Stewart-Way class III), the injury was recognised during the operation, a closed drain was placed to the gallbladder fossa, and the decision was drain-and-refer to a hepatobiliary team (theatre_link, C16).
Jaundice first noted on postoperative day 2 and deepening since; dark urine and pale stools from day 3; mild itching (case data).
No new regular medications; perioperative cefazolin only (case data).
Eating and drinking; bowels working; afebrile throughout the postoperative course (case data).

presentation_stages.narrative: The patient is assessed at the hepatobiliary referral centre on postoperative day 4 after the index laparoscopic cholecystectomy whose Theatre debrief (trace-02) records a recognised common bile duct transection, a drain placed, and a drain-and-refer decision. She is visibly jaundiced, with dark urine, pale stools and mild itching. She is afebrile (36.9 C), heart rate 78/min, blood pressure 122/74 mmHg. The closed drain to the gallbladder fossa placed at the index operation drains about 40 mL per 24 h of bile-stained fluid, falling each day. Abdomen soft, mild right upper quadrant discomfort, no peritonism. The learner must commit a stage-1 differential board for post-cholecystectomy jaundice before any new result exists.
presentation_stages.title: Postoperative day 4 — referral-centre assessment

presentation_stages.narrative: Laboratories: total bilirubin 6.8 mg/dL; alkaline phosphatase 520 U/L (about four times the upper limit of reference); ALT 96 U/L and AST 88 U/L (each under three times the upper limit); white cell count 8.9 x10^9/L; CRP 8 mg/L — below the TG18 cholangitis inflammatory-response threshold; platelets 268 x10^9/L. Ultrasound: intrahepatic bile ducts are dilated; no subhepatic or intra-abdominal fluid collection; the distal common bile duct is incompletely visualised and no stone is identified in it.
presentation_stages.title: Laboratory panel and abdominal ultrasound

presentation_stages.narrative: ERCP (ordered by the learner at stage 2 with therapeutic intent for a presumed retained stone): the cholangiogram opacifies a normal-calibre distal common bile duct up to an abrupt cut-off at surgical clips in the mid common bile duct. No contrast passes the clips; the proximal biliary tree is not opacified (ERCP cannot show ducts upstream of a complete obstruction, C14). No stone is seen in the distal duct and none is extracted. No sphincterotomy or stent is possible across a complete transection.
presentation_stages.title: ERCP — the learner's order returns

presentation_stages.narrative: MRCP (the gold standard for complete morphological evaluation of the biliary tree, C14): complete transection of the common bile duct at the clip level; the remaining common hepatic duct stump measures 25 mm below an intact hepatic duct confluence; intrahepatic ducts are dilated above the injury; no stone is present in any duct; no injury to an aberrant right sectoral duct; the injury is complete (circumferential), not a lateral defect; no leak from the cystic duct stump or any minor duct; no fluid collection. The Strasberg–Bismuth classification is computed from these findings by the case's classification block. Adjudication and the WSES-timed disposition follow.
presentation_stages.title: MRCP — definitive anatomy, classification, disposition

case.synthetic_note: Synthetic case, authored for teaching. The patient is the same authored fiction as case.ruq-pain.001; her operation is the Theatre's shipped trace-02 attempt (Milestone 17), whose debrief file is this case's operative-history evidence (see theatre_link). No real patient data exists in this module.

theatre_link.note: Every value in matched_fields is read from the shipped debrief file by the checker and compared field by field, and the file's SHA-256 is recomputed. Nothing in this case's operative history is retyped from the Milestone 17 report: if the debrief file changes, this case's checks fail until the case is re-derived.
theatre_link.role: Operative history — THE LOOP. This case's index operation is the Theatre's shipped trace-02 attempt, and its debrief is this case's stage-1 operative-history evidence. Design/07's interchange section specifies exactly this: 'Theatre post-op complications generate case stubs in the same format (the missed bile-duct injury returns as a case), closing the loop between modules.'

case.title: Postoperative jaundice, day 4 after laparoscopic cholecystectomy — the trace-02 bile duct injury returns

validity.consequences: Scores are formative feedback only; no credentialing, progression, or clinical decision may rest on them.
validity.internal_structure: Component scores derived from the case model by stated rules (cases/parameters.json); no composite score is computed, because design/07 defines components (Brier-style calibration, anchoring, evidence quality) and no weights. Calibration proper needs a case series; two cases yield two sets of staged scores, and the debrief says so.
